title: Username path gets truncated, causing PowerToys to create config files in a wrong C:\Users\<truncated_name> folder
summary: The historical Mouse Without Borders LocalAppData use-after-free is already fixed in current and v0.100.2 source. The remaining command-line quoting risk does not explain the reported one-character truncation, so a current-version reproduction is required before a defensible fix design.

status.label: Needs current reproduction
status.detail: Request current-version diagnostics before designing a fix.

judgment.rationale: The historical Mouse Without Borders LocalAppData use-after-free is already fixed in current and v0.100.2 source. The remaining command-line quoting risk does not explain the reported one-character truncation, so a current-version reproduction is required before a defensible fix design.
evidence: Current source copies SHGetKnownFolderPath output through wil::unique_cotaskmem_string before the buffer is released.
The historical use-after-free could corrupt a profile path, but that implementation is not present in the reported v0.100.2 source.
The remaining unquoted LocalAppData service argument is a hardening concern for whitespace or quotes, not evidence for truncating a numeric username by one character.
judgment.recommended_action: Request a fresh latest-version reproduction and diagnostics that preserve the service command-line argument boundaries.

actions.label: Request current reproduction and profile-path diagnostics

comment.body: The historical profile-path lifetime defect is already fixed in the current and reported source, so we need a fresh reproduction before changing a different path boundary. Please update to the latest stable PowerToys release and confirm whether the truncated profile-directory behavior still occurs. If it does, attach a newly generated PowerToys bug report ZIP and provide the exact Windows user-profile path, the unexpected directory path created, installation scope, whether Mouse Without Borders is enabled, and the approximate time of reproduction. Please also include the service command line from Windows Services with personal values redacted, preserving quotation and argument boundaries.
